texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.Why do you want to join Cryptio specific: I have spent a decade at the intersection Cryptio sits on: crypto infrastructure that has to satisfy accountants, banks and regulators. At Everex (Singapore) I was Chief Engineer for Lending & Risk Management and led government/bank relations across SE Asia on structuring crypto payments and stablecoins. As co-founder of Platinum VC & Incubator ($35M under management, portfolio ~70% crypto) I have run partnerships as a system for 11 years: 2,000+ institutional-investor calls, a self-built CRM that up to 30 operators used daily - today automated with AI agents. Growth Owner - Partnerships is the motion I already run every day: map the ecosystem, activate partners one concrete deal at a time, instrument every step. I also bring my own distribution: a 169k-subscriber Telegram channel and a 500+ AI-practitioner community in Palo Alto.
texts.Which custodians do you have live relati: Honest answer: no live custodian relationships today. My crypto network was built on the adjacent side - partnerships with hedge funds, market makers and brokers from shipping crypto-exchange infrastructure, plus bank and government relations across SE Asia from Everex (structuring crypto payments and stablecoins). I run partnerships as a CRM-instrumented system with 2,000+ institutional-investor calls behind me, so building a live custodian map (the Fireblocks / BitGo / Copper tier) is my first 90-day sprint, not a cold start.
texts.Give us one partnership you activated, w: The Platinum VC syndicate. Before: no fund - deal-by-deal fundraising for portfolio startups. After: $35M under management and a standing syndicate of 250 VCs/angels, fed by 2,000+ qualified institutional-investor calls and a self-built CRM used daily by up to 30 operators. The activation motion each time: qualify, enrich, bring the partner a concrete first deal, then keep them warm on an automated follow-up cadence.
texts.A partner's gone quiet on referrals. Wha: 1) Diagnose before pinging: pull the CRM history - last referral, last touch, what changed on their side (team, priorities, a deal that went sideways). 2) Re-deliver value first: bring them something concrete - a warm intro, a client for them, refreshed materials - so the next touch is a gift, not a chase. 3) Change the channel and the altitude: move from email to a short call or in-person, ask directly what a good referral looks like for them now, and put them on an instrumented cadence so silence gets caught in days, not quarters.
texts.Is there anything else you'd like us to: US O-1 visa active (no sponsorship needed, now or in the future) and EU citizen - the New York role works from either side. Available immediately. I automate my own partnerships work with AI agents (public production fleet at github.com/tonydzi), so you get a partnerships owner who also builds his own tooling.
